source_refs.note: Exercise 13.2, Question 1 (i)-(xi): differentiate w.r.t. x (book p.254-255). (ii) and (vi) are garbled in print; read from the answer key (PDF 311). Key labels (viii) as (vii).

blocks.explanation:
Yeh sab se seedha qism ka sawal hai: \(x\) ki powers ka jama (sum).
Humein \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) find karna hai, yani function ka derivative.
Plan: har term ko alag alag differentiate karenge, sum rule, constant multiple rule aur power rule laga kar, phir jawab jama kar denge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = x^4 + 2x^3 + x^2\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: Sum ka derivative har term ke derivative ka sum hota hai (theorem 4). Constant (jaise 2) bahar hi rehta hai (theorem 3). Aur power rule: \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^n) = nx^{n-1}\). Yeh teen rules is liye kaafi hain ke har term sirf ek number guna \(x\) ki power hai.

Har term ko alag differentiate karein
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{d}{dx}(x^4) + 2\frac{d}{dx}(x^3) + \frac{d}{dx}(x^2)\]
Kyun: Sum rule humein ijazat deta hai ke lambi expression ko tukron mein tor dein. \(2x^3\) mein 2 ek constant hai, is liye woh derivative ke bahar aa jata hai aur sirf \(x^3\) ko differentiate karna parta hai.

Power rule lagayein
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = 4x^3 + 2(3x^2) + 2x\]
\[= 4x^3 + 6x^2 + 2x\]
Kyun: Power rule ka matlab hai: power ko neeche utaar kar aage likh do, aur power mein se 1 kam kar do. \(x^4\) se \(4x^3\), \(x^3\) se \(3x^2\), aur \(x^2\) se \(2x\) bana. Phir \(2 \times 3x^2 = 6x^2\).
Dhyan dein: Power kam karna na bhoolein; \(x^4\) ka derivative \(4x^4\) likhna aam ghalti hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\text{At } x = 1:\ 4 + 6 + 2 = 12\]
\[\frac{y(1.001) - y(0.999)}{0.002} \approx 12.00\]
Kyun: Derivative asal mein curve ka slope hai. Agar \(x = 1\) ke bilkul qareeb do points le kar slope nikalein to wohi 12 aata hai jo formula deta hai. Is se pakka ho jata hai ke jawab sahi hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Differentiate w.r.t. \(x\): \(x^{-3} + 2x^{-3/2} + 3\) [printed as \(x^{-3} + 2x - \frac{3}{2} + 3\); the exponent \(-\frac{3}{2}\) has slipped onto the line]
blocks.explanation:
Yahan bhi \(x\) ki powers ka sum hai, lekin powers negative aur fraction wali hain.
Humein \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) find karna hai.
Ghabrane ki zaroorat nahi: power rule har real power ke liye chalta hai, chahe power negative ho ya fraction.
Plan: har term par power rule, aur constant ka derivative zero.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = x^{-3} + 2x^{-3/2} + 3\). Kitab mein beech wali term ki power \(-\frac{3}{2}\) line par gir gayi hai; answer key se pata chalta hai ke asal function yahi hai (neeche "Kitab ki ghalti" dekhein).
Humein find karna hai: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: Sum rule, constant multiple rule, power rule \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^n) = nx^{n-1}\) (kitab ke Note ke mutabiq har real \(n\) ke liye), aur \(\frac{d}{dx}(c) = 0\).

\(x^{-3}\) ko differentiate karein
\[\frac{d}{dx}(x^{-3}) = -3x^{-3-1} = -3x^{-4}\]
Kyun: Power rule mein \(n = -3\). Power neeche aayi to \(-3\) aage likha gaya, aur power mein se 1 minus kiya: \(-3 - 1 = -4\).
Dhyan dein: Negative power mein 1 kam karne se number aur chhota (zyada negative) hota hai. \(-3 - 1 = -4\) hai, \(-2\) nahi; yeh bohat aam ghalti hai.

\(2x^{-3/2}\) ko differentiate karein
\[\frac{d}{dx}(2x^{-3/2}) = 2\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)x^{-\frac{3}{2}-1}\]
\[= -3x^{-5/2}\]
Kyun: Yahan \(n = -\frac{3}{2}\) hai. \(-\frac{3}{2} - 1 = -\frac{3}{2} - \frac{2}{2} = -\frac{5}{2}\). Aage wala 2 aur fraction ka 2 cancel ho gaye, is liye sirf \(-3\) bacha.

Constant ka derivative aur sab ka jama
\[\frac{d}{dx}(3) = 0\]
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = -3x^{-4} - 3x^{-5/2}\]
\[= -3\left(\dfrac{1}{x^4} + \dfrac{1}{x^{5/2}}\right)\]
Kyun: Constant kabhi badalta nahi, is liye us ka rate of change (tabdeeli ki raftaar) zero hai. Aakhir mein \(-3\) common nikala to bilkul answer key wali shakal aa gayi; negative power ko fraction mein likhna \(x^{-4} = \frac{1}{x^4}\) wala qaida hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\text{At } x = 1:\ -3(1 + 1) = -6\]
\[\frac{y(1.001) - y(0.999)}{0.002} \approx -6.00\]
Kyun: \(x = 1\) ke qareeb do points se nikala hua slope bhi \(-6\) hai, jo formula se mel khata hai. Is tarah calculator se chhota sa check exam mein bhi kaam aata hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein part (ii) \(x^{-3} + 2x - \frac{3}{2} + 3\) chhapa hai: beech wali term ki power \(-\frac{3}{2}\) upar ke bajaye line par aa gayi hai. Agar isay waise hi parhein to derivative \(-3x^{-4} + 2\) banta. Lekin answer key ka jawab \(-3\left(\frac{1}{x^4} + \frac{1}{x^{5/2}}\right)\) sirf \(x^{-3} + 2x^{-3/2} + 3\) ka derivative hai, is liye humne yahi sahi function le kar hal kiya.

blocks.explanation:
Yahan ek function doosre se divide ho raha hai, aur yeh fraction simplify nahi hoti.
Humein \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) find karna hai.
Jab upar aur neeche dono mein \(x\) ho to quotient rule (taqseem ka qaida) lagta hai.
Plan: upar \(f(x) = 2x - 3\), neeche \(g(x) = 2x + 1\); dono ke derivatives nikal kar formula mein rakhenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \dfrac{2x - 3}{2x + 1}\), \(x \ne -\frac{1}{2}\) (warna neeche zero aa jayega).
Humein find karna hai: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: Quotient rule (theorem 6): \(\left(\frac{f}{g}\right)' = \frac{f'g - fg'}{g^2}\). Upar aur neeche ko alag alag differentiate kar ke divide karna ghalat hai; isi liye yeh formula banaya gaya hai.

Hissay alag karein
\[f(x) = 2x - 3,\ f'(x) = 2\]
\[g(x) = 2x + 1,\ g'(x) = 2\]
Kyun: \(2x\) ka derivative 2 hai aur constant ka zero. Pehle yeh chaar cheezein alag likh lena formula mein ghalti ka chance kam kar deta hai.

Quotient rule lagayein
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2(2x + 1) - (2x - 3)(2)}{(2x + 1)^2}\]
Kyun: Yaad rakhne ka tareeqa: "neeche wala guna upar ka derivative, minus upar wala guna neeche ka derivative, sab taqseem neeche ka square". Minus sign ki wajah se tarteeb (order) bohat zaroori hai; ulta likhenge to jawab ka sign ulta ho jayega.

Numerator simplify karein
\[2(2x + 1) - 2(2x - 3)\]
\[= 4x + 2 - 4x + 6 = 8\]
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{8}{(2x + 1)^2}\]
Kyun: Doosri bracket ke aage minus hai, is liye us ki har term ka sign badlega: \(-2 \times (-3) = +6\). \(4x\) aur \(-4x\) cancel ho gaye aur sirf 8 bacha.
Dhyan dein: Neeche ka \((2x + 1)^2\) expand karne ki zaroorat nahi; usay waise hi rehne dein.

Tasdeeq
\[\text{At } x = 0:\ \frac{8}{1} = 8\]
\[\frac{y(0.001) - y(-0.001)}{0.002} \approx 8.00\]
Kyun: \(x = 0\) ke qareeb numerical slope bhi 8 aaya, to formula sahi hai.

blocks.explanation:
Yahan product ko \(\sqrt{x}\) se divide kiya gaya hai. Seedha quotient rule lagayein to kaam bohat lamba ho jayega.
Humein \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) find karna hai.
Samajhdari yeh hai ke pehle expression ko simplify karein, phir differentiate.
Plan: \(\sqrt{x}\) se divide, brackets multiply, phir power rule.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \dfrac{(1 + \sqrt{x})(x - x^{3/2})}{\sqrt{x}}\), \(x > 0\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: Root ko power ki shakal mein likhenge (\(\sqrt{x} = x^{1/2}\)), simplify kar ke powers ka sum banayenge, phir har term par power rule. Jab simplification mumkin ho to hamesha pehle simplify karein; differentiation chhoti aur ghalti se paak ho jati hai.

Doosri bracket ko \(\sqrt{x}\) se divide karein
\[\dfrac{x - x^{3/2}}{x^{1/2}} = x^{1/2} - x\]
Kyun: Indices ka qaida \(\frac{x^m}{x^n} = x^{m-n}\). \(\frac{x}{x^{1/2}} = x^{1 - 1/2} = x^{1/2}\), aur \(\frac{x^{3/2}}{x^{1/2}} = x^{3/2 - 1/2} = x^1 = x\). Denominator ek hi term hai, is liye har term ko alag divide kar sakte hain.

Brackets multiply karein
\[y = (1 + x^{1/2})(x^{1/2} - x)\]
\[= x^{1/2} - x + x - x^{3/2}\]
\[= x^{1/2} - x^{3/2}\]
Kyun: \(1\) ko dono terms se guna kiya, phir \(x^{1/2}\) ko: \(x^{1/2} \cdot x^{1/2} = x^1\) aur \(x^{1/2} \cdot x = x^{3/2}\) (powers jama hoti hain). \(-x\) aur \(+x\) cancel ho gaye. Dekhiye, itni bari expression sirf do terms reh gayi!

Differentiate karein
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{2}x^{-1/2} - \frac{3}{2}x^{1/2}\]
Kyun: Power rule: \(x^{1/2}\) ka derivative \(\frac{1}{2}x^{1/2 - 1} = \frac{1}{2}x^{-1/2}\), aur \(x^{3/2}\) ka \(\frac{3}{2}x^{1/2}\).

Ek fraction banayein
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} - \dfrac{3\sqrt{x}}{2}\]
\[= \dfrac{1 - 3x}{2\sqrt{x}}\]
Kyun: \(x^{-1/2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\). Common denominator \(2\sqrt{x}\) lene ke liye doosri term ko upar neeche \(\sqrt{x}\) se guna kiya: \(\sqrt{x} \cdot \sqrt{x} = x\). Is tarah answer key wali shakal aa gayi.
Dhyan dein: \(\sqrt{x}\sqrt{x} = x\) hai, \(2\sqrt{x}\) nahi.

Tasdeeq
\[\text{At } x = 1:\ \frac{1 - 3}{2} = -1\]
\[\frac{y(1.001) - y(0.999)}{0.002} \approx -1.00\]
Kyun: \(x = 1\) ke qareeb numerical slope bhi \(-1\) hai, is liye jawab sahi hai.

blocks.explanation:
Yeh ek bracket ka square hai.
Humein \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) find karna hai.
Bracket ke andar root aur fraction hain, lekin square khol dene se sab kuch \(x\) ki powers ban jata hai.
Plan: \((a - b)^2\) wala formula, powers ki shakal, phir power rule.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \left(\sqrt{x} - \dfrac{1}{x}\right)^2\), \(x > 0\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: \((a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2\) se square kholenge, har term ko \(x\) ki power likhenge, phir term by term differentiate. Chain rule ki zaroorat hi nahi parti agar pehle expand kar lein.

Square kholein
\[y = (\sqrt{x})^2 - 2\sqrt{x} \cdot \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{x^2}\]
\[= x - 2x^{-1/2} + x^{-2}\]
Kyun: \(a = \sqrt{x}\) aur \(b = \frac{1}{x}\) liye. \((\sqrt{x})^2 = x\). Beech wali term: \(\frac{\sqrt{x}}{x} = \frac{x^{1/2}}{x^1} = x^{-1/2}\). Aakhri: \(\frac{1}{x^2} = x^{-2}\).
Dhyan dein: Beech wali term \(-2ab\) bhoolna sab se aam ghalti hai; \((a - b)^2\) kabhi bhi \(a^2 - b^2\) nahi hota.

Term by term differentiate karein
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = 1 - 2\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)x^{-3/2} + (-2)x^{-3}\]
\[= 1 + x^{-3/2} - 2x^{-3}\]
Kyun: \(x\) ka derivative 1. \(-2x^{-1/2}\) par power rule: \(-2 \times (-\frac{1}{2}) = +1\) aur power \(-\frac{1}{2} - 1 = -\frac{3}{2}\). \(x^{-2}\) ka derivative \(-2x^{-3}\). Do minus mil kar plus bane, is par khaas dhyan dein.

Tasdeeq
\[\text{At } x = 1:\ 1 + 1 - 2 = 0\]
\[\frac{y(1.001) - y(0.999)}{0.002} \approx 0.00\]
Kyun: \(x = 1\) par bracket \(1 - 1 = 0\) hai, aur square ki sab se chhoti value zero hoti hai. Sab se nichle point par curve ka slope zero hota hai, aur humara formula bhi wahan zero de raha hai. Yeh khoobsurat check hai!

blocks.prompt: 1 (vi) Differentiate w.r.t. \(x\): \((x - 5)(3 - x)\) [printed as \((x\ \ 5)(3\ \ x)\): both operation signs are missing]
blocks.explanation:
Yeh do linear brackets ka product (hasil-e-zarb) hai.
Humein \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) find karna hai.
Product rule bhi lag sakta hai aur pehle multiply kar ke power rule bhi; dono se ek hi jawab aayega.
Plan: product rule se hal karenge aur expand kar ke check karenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = (x - 5)(3 - x)\). Kitab mein dono brackets ke andar ke nishan (signs) chhape hi nahi; sirf yahi reading answer key \(8 - 2x\) se milti hai (neeche "Kitab ki ghalti" dekhein).
Humein find karna hai: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: Product rule (theorem 5): \((fg)' = f'g + fg'\), jahan \(f = x - 5\) aur \(g = 3 - x\).

Hissay alag karein
\[f = x - 5,\ f' = 1\]
\[g = 3 - x,\ g' = -1\]
Kyun: \(x\) ka derivative 1, \(-x\) ka \(-1\), aur constant (5 ya 3) ka zero.
Dhyan dein: \(3 - x\) ka derivative \(+1\) likhna aam ghalti hai; \(x\) ke saath minus hai, to derivative bhi minus wala hoga.

Product rule lagayein
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = (1)(3 - x) + (x - 5)(-1)\]
\[= 3 - x - x + 5\]
\[= 8 - 2x\]
Kyun: Product rule kehta hai: pehle ka derivative guna doosra, jama pehla guna doosre ka derivative. Do functions ke product ka derivative sirf dono derivatives ka product nahi hota (\(1 \times (-1) = -1\) ghalat jawab hota). \(-(x - 5) = -x + 5\) mein sign ka khayal rakhein.

Tasdeeq: pehle expand kar ke
\[y = 3x - x^2 - 15 + 5x = -x^2 + 8x - 15\]
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = -2x + 8\]
Kyun: Doosre tareeqe se bhi bilkul wohi jawab aaya. Exam mein agar waqt ho to aise chhote sawal dono tareeqon se check kar lein.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein part (vi) \((x\ \ 5)(3\ \ x)\) chhapa hai, dono brackets ke andar plus ya minus ka nishan ghayab hai. Chaar mumkin readings hain: \((x + 5)(3 + x)\), \((x + 5)(3 - x)\), \((x - 5)(3 + x)\) aur \((x - 5)(3 - x)\). Inke derivatives \(2x + 8\), \(-2x - 2\), \(2x - 2\) aur \(8 - 2x\) bante hain. Answer key \(8 - 2x\) deti hai, jo sirf \((x - 5)(3 - x)\) ka derivative hai, is liye humne yahi liya.

blocks.explanation:
Yeh quotient hai, aur upar ek bracket ka square hai.
Humein \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) find karna hai.
Upar wale square ko pehle khol lein to us ka derivative sirf power rule se mil jata hai.
Plan: upar expand, quotient rule, aur aakhir mein common factor nikal kar jawab chhota karna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \dfrac{(x^2 + 1)^2}{x^2 - 1}\), \(x \ne \pm 1\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: Quotient rule \(\left(\frac{f}{g}\right)' = \frac{f'g - fg'}{g^2}\), jahan \(f = (x^2 + 1)^2\) aur \(g = x^2 - 1\). Upar aur neeche dono mein \(x\) hai aur cancel bhi nahi hota, is liye quotient rule zaroori hai.

Upar wale ka derivative
\[f = x^4 + 2x^2 + 1\]
\[f' = 4x^3 + 4x = 4x(x^2 + 1)\]
Kyun: \((a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2\) se \((x^2 + 1)^2 = x^4 + 2x^2 + 1\). Ab har term par power rule. Phir \(4x\) common nikala, kyunke aage factorise karne mein yahi \((x^2 + 1)\) kaam aayega.

Neeche wale ka derivative
\[g = x^2 - 1,\ g' = 2x\]
Kyun: \(x^2\) ka derivative \(2x\), constant ka zero.

Quotient rule lagayein
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{4x(x^2 + 1)(x^2 - 1) - (x^2 + 1)^2(2x)}{(x^2 - 1)^2}\]
Kyun: Formula ki tarteeb: \(f'g\) pehle, phir minus \(fg'\), aur neeche \(g^2\).

Common factor \(2x(x^2 + 1)\) nikalein
\[\text{Num} = 2x(x^2 + 1)[2(x^2 - 1) - (x^2 + 1)]\]
\[= 2x(x^2 + 1)(x^2 - 3)\]
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2x(x^2 + 1)(x^2 - 3)}{(x^2 - 1)^2}\]
Kyun: Dono terms mein \(2x\) aur \((x^2 + 1)\) mojood hain. Inhein bahar nikalne se andar sirf \(2x^2 - 2 - x^2 - 1 = x^2 - 3\) bachta hai. Agar sab kuch multiply kar dete to degree 5 ki lambi expression banti aur ghalti ka khatra barhta.
Dhyan dein: Bracket \((x^2 + 1)\) ke aage minus hai, to \(-x^2 - 1\) likhein, \(-x^2 + 1\) nahi.

Tasdeeq
\[\text{At } x = 2:\ \frac{2(2)(5)(1)}{9} = \frac{20}{9} \approx 2.222\]
\[\frac{y(2.001) - y(1.999)}{0.002} \approx 2.222\]
Kyun: \(x = 2\) par numerical slope formula se mil gaya, is liye jawab sahi hai.

blocks.explanation:
Do quadratic expressions ka quotient hai.
Humein \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) find karna hai.
Plan: quotient rule lagayenge aur numerator mein \(2x\) common nikal kar simplify karenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \dfrac{x^2 + 1}{x^2 - 3}\), \(x \ne \pm\sqrt{3}\) (wahan neeche zero hota hai).
Humein find karna hai: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: Quotient rule, \(f = x^2 + 1\) aur \(g = x^2 - 3\).

Hissay alag karein
\[f' = 2x,\ g' = 2x\]
Kyun: Dono mein \(x^2\) ka derivative \(2x\) hai; 1 aur \(-3\) constants hain, un ka derivative zero.

Quotient rule lagayein
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2x(x^2 - 3) - (x^2 + 1)(2x)}{(x^2 - 3)^2}\]
Kyun: Neeche guna upar ka derivative, minus upar guna neeche ka derivative, sab taqseem neeche ka square.

Numerator simplify karein
\[2x[(x^2 - 3) - (x^2 + 1)] = 2x(-4)\]
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{-8x}{(x^2 - 3)^2}\]
Kyun: \(2x\) dono terms mein hai, us ko bahar nikala. Andar \(x^2 - 3 - x^2 - 1\) bacha, jahan \(x^2\) cancel ho gaya aur \(-4\) reh gaya. \(2x \times (-4) = -8x\).
Dhyan dein: Doosri bracket se pehle minus hai, is liye \(+1\) bhi \(-1\) ban jata hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\text{At } x = 1:\ \frac{-8}{4} = -2\]
\[\frac{y(1.001) - y(0.999)}{0.002} \approx -2.00\]
Kyun: Numerical slope formula se milta hai, to jawab sahi hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key mein is part ka jawab \(\frac{-8x}{(x^2 - 3)^2}\) doosri dafa "(vii)" ke label ke saath chhapa hai; asal mein yeh part (viii) ka jawab hai. Jawab khud sahi hai, sirf label ghalat hai.

blocks.explanation:
Yeh quotient hai, aur neeche ek bracket ka square root hai.
Humein \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) find karna hai.
Naya kaam sirf \(\sqrt{x^2 + 1}\) ka derivative hai; baaqi wohi quotient rule.
Plan: root ka derivative, quotient rule, phir numerator ki chhoti fraction khatam karna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \dfrac{2x - 1}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}\) (neeche kabhi zero nahi hota, kyunke \(x^2 + 1 \ge 1\)).
Humein find karna hai: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: Quotient rule, \(f = 2x - 1\) aur \(g = \sqrt{x^2 + 1}\). \(g'\) ke liye bracket ke root ka derivative chahiye.

Bracket ke root ka derivative
\[\frac{d}{dx}\sqrt{u} = \dfrac{u'}{2\sqrt{u}}\]
Kyun: Kitab ne root ke andar bracket wala qaida (chain rule) nahi diya, is liye hum isay definition se samajh lete hain. Conjugate se guna karne par \(\sqrt{u(x + \delta x)} - \sqrt{u(x)} = \dfrac{u(x + \delta x) - u(x)}{\sqrt{u(x + \delta x)} + \sqrt{u(x)}}\) banta hai. Ab \(\delta x\) se divide kar ke \(\delta x \to 0\) karein: upar \(u'\) ban jata hai aur neeche \(\sqrt{u} + \sqrt{u} = 2\sqrt{u}\). Simple misaal: \(u = x\) lein to \(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\) aata hai, jo power rule se bhi yahi hai.

Hissay alag karein
\[f' = 2\]
\[g' = \dfrac{2x}{2\sqrt{x^2 + 1}} = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}\]
Kyun: Root wale qaide mein \(u = x^2 + 1\) aur \(u' = 2x\) rakha; 2 cancel ho gaya.
Dhyan dein: \(\sqrt{x^2 + 1}\) ka derivative \(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}\) likh dena (andar ka derivative \(2x\) bhool jana) sab se aam ghalti hai.

Quotient rule lagayein
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{x^2 + 1} - (2x - 1)\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}}{x^2 + 1}\]
Kyun: \(f'g - fg'\) upar, aur neeche \(g^2 = (\sqrt{x^2 + 1})^2 = x^2 + 1\); square aur root ek doosre ko khatam kar dete hain.

Upar neeche \(\sqrt{x^2 + 1}\) se guna karein
\[\text{Num} = 2(x^2 + 1) - x(2x - 1)\]
\[= 2x^2 + 2 - 2x^2 + x = x + 2\]
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x + 2}{(x^2 + 1)^{3/2}}\]
Kyun: Numerator ke andar fraction thi; upar neeche ek hi cheez se guna karne se value nahi badalti magar fraction khatam ho jati hai. Neeche \((x^2 + 1)^1 \cdot (x^2 + 1)^{1/2} = (x^2 + 1)^{3/2}\), kyunke powers jama hoti hain.

Tasdeeq
\[\text{At } x = 0:\ \frac{2}{1} = 2\]
\[\frac{y(0.001) - y(-0.001)}{0.002} \approx 2.00\]
Kyun: \(x = 0\) par numerical slope bhi 2 hai, is liye jawab sahi hai.

blocks.explanation:
Yeh ek fraction ka square root hai, aur \(a\) ek constant hai (us ka derivative zero).
Humein \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) find karna hai.
Bari root ko do chhoti roots mein tor dena aasaan rasta hai.
Plan: \(\frac{\sqrt{a - x}}{\sqrt{a + x}}\) likh kar quotient rule aur root wala qaida, phir simplify.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \sqrt{\dfrac{a - x}{a + x}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{a - x}}{\sqrt{a + x}}\), jahan \(-a < x < a\) aur \(a > 0\) (taake root ke andar positive ho).
Humein find karna hai: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: Quotient rule, \(f = \sqrt{a - x}\), \(g = \sqrt{a + x}\), aur root ka qaida \(\frac{d}{dx}\sqrt{u} = \frac{u'}{2\sqrt{u}}\). Fraction ka root upar aur neeche ke root ki fraction ke barabar hota hai, is liye yeh torna jaiz hai.

Hissay alag karein
\[f' = \dfrac{-1}{2\sqrt{a - x}}\]
\[g' = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{a + x}}\]
Kyun: Root wala qaida (part (ix) mein definition se samjhaya). \(u = a - x\) ka derivative \(-1\) hai, kyunke \(a\) constant hai aur \(-x\) ka derivative \(-1\). \(u = a + x\) ka derivative \(+1\).
Dhyan dein: \(\sqrt{a - x}\) ke derivative mein minus aata hai; yeh minus bhoolne se poora jawab ghalat ho jata hai.

Quotient rule lagayein
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{-\dfrac{\sqrt{a + x}}{2\sqrt{a - x}} - \dfrac{\sqrt{a - x}}{2\sqrt{a + x}}}{a + x}\]
Kyun: \(f'g\) pehli term, \(fg'\) doosri term, aur neeche \(g^2 = (\sqrt{a + x})^2 = a + x\).

Numerator ko common denominator \(2\sqrt{a - x}\sqrt{a + x}\) par layein
\[\text{Num} = \dfrac{-(a + x) - (a - x)}{2\sqrt{a - x}\sqrt{a + x}}\]
\[= \dfrac{-2a}{2\sqrt{a - x}\sqrt{a + x}}\]
Kyun: Pehli fraction ko upar neeche \(\sqrt{a + x}\) se aur doosri ko \(\sqrt{a - x}\) se guna kiya; root guna root = andar wali cheez. Phir \(-a - x - a + x = -2a\); \(x\) cancel ho gaya.

\(a + x\) se divide karein
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{-a}{\sqrt{a - x}\,(a + x)\sqrt{a + x}}\]
\[= \dfrac{-a}{\sqrt{a - x}\,(a + x)^{3/2}}\]
Kyun: 2 cancel hua. Neeche \((a + x)^1 \cdot (a + x)^{1/2} = (a + x)^{3/2}\). Yahi answer key wali shakal hai.

Tasdeeq
\[a = 3,\ x = 1:\ \frac{-3}{\sqrt{2} \cdot 8} \approx -0.2652\]
\[\frac{y(1.001) - y(0.999)}{0.002} \approx -0.2652\]
Kyun: Misaal ke taur par \(a = 3\) le kar \(x = 1\) ke qareeb numerical slope nikala; formula se bilkul mel khata hai.

blocks.explanation:
Yahan upar bhi root hai aur neeche bhi, dono ke andar bracket.
Humein \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) find karna hai.
Yeh part (ix) aur (x) ka hi milta julta sawal hai.
Plan: dono roots ke derivatives root wale qaide se, quotient rule, phir fraction ke andar ki fraction ko saaf karna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}{\sqrt{x^2 - 1}}\), jahan \(|x| > 1\) (taake neeche ka root real aur non-zero ho).
Humein find karna hai: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: Quotient rule, \(f = \sqrt{x^2 + 1}\), \(g = \sqrt{x^2 - 1}\), aur \(\frac{d}{dx}\sqrt{u} = \frac{u'}{2\sqrt{u}}\).

Hissay alag karein
\[f' = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}\]
\[g' = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^2 - 1}}\]
Kyun: Root wala qaida (part (ix) mein samjhaya). Dono mein andar wale ka derivative \(2x\) hai, aur \(\frac{2x}{2} = x\).

Quotient rule lagayein
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\dfrac{x\sqrt{x^2 - 1}}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}} - \dfrac{x\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}{\sqrt{x^2 - 1}}}{x^2 - 1}\]
Kyun: \(f'g = \frac{x}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}} \cdot \sqrt{x^2 - 1}\) aur \(fg' = \sqrt{x^2 + 1} \cdot \frac{x}{\sqrt{x^2 - 1}}\); neeche \(g^2 = x^2 - 1\).

Numerator ko common denominator par layein
\[\text{Num} = \dfrac{x(x^2 - 1) - x(x^2 + 1)}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}\sqrt{x^2 - 1}}\]
\[= \dfrac{-2x}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}\sqrt{x^2 - 1}}\]
Kyun: Pehli term ko upar neeche \(\sqrt{x^2 - 1}\) se aur doosri ko \(\sqrt{x^2 + 1}\) se guna kiya, taake dono ka denominator ek ho jaye. Phir \(x^3 - x - x^3 - x = -2x\).
Dhyan dein: \(-x(x^2 + 1) = -x^3 - x\); doosri term ka sign bhi badalna hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\text{At } x = 2:\ \frac{-4}{\sqrt{5} \cdot 3\sqrt{3}} \approx -0.3443\]
\[\frac{y(2.001) - y(1.999)}{0.002} \approx -0.3443\]
Kyun: \(x = 2\) par numerical slope formula se milta hai. Negative slope ka matlab hai ke \(x\) barhne se \(y\) kam ho raha hai; waqai \(x\) bara ho to \(y\) 1 ke qareeb aata jata hai.
